lines: 榜单上的分数年年创新高，实际用起来却还是会出错。
Scores climb every year, yet real use still goes wrong.
这不是模型突然变笨，而是分数和能力之间有一道缝。
The model did not get dumber. A gap sits between score and ability.
这一章要回答：我们到底怎么知道一个模型行不行。
This chapter asks how we can actually tell whether a model works.
先说结论：分数是能力的代理指标，不是能力本身。
First, the claim: a score is a proxy, not ability itself.
记住这句话，后面每一节都在给它加注脚。
Hold that line. Every section after this adds a footnote to it.
我们可以精确测量损失，但损失低不等于好用。
We can measure loss precisely, but low loss is not usefulness.
损失衡量的是对下一个词的预测有多准。
Loss measures how well the next word is predicted.
而人关心的是，它能不能帮我把问题解决掉。
What people care about is whether it solves the problem.
损失降低零点一，普通用户能感知到差别吗。
Loss drops by 0.1. Does any user feel the difference?
MMLU 提高两分，意味着它更会写代码吗。
MMLU rises two points. Does it write better code?
聊天机器人在榜单上很强，用起来为什么还是笨。
It tops the charts. So why is it still dumb in practice?
基准的演化史，就是一场出题人和模型的军备竞赛。
Benchmark history is an arms race between test writers and models.
二零一八年 GLUE 考句子级理解，一共九个任务。
In 2018 GLUE tested sentence-level understanding with nine tasks.
二零二一年 MMLU 用五十七个学科、约一点四万道选择题考世界知识。
In 2021 MMLU used 57 subjects and about 14,000 multiple-choice questions.
同年 GSM8K 考小学应用题，约八千五百道。
That year GSM8K added grade-school word problems, about 8,500.
HumanEval 只有一百六十四道手写 Python 函数题。
HumanEval had only 164 hand-written Python function tasks.
二零二五年 HLE 两千五百题，专家出，号称搜索不到。
In 2025 HLE arrived: 2,500 expert questions said to be unsearchable.
发布时前沿模型的准确率，只有个位数。
Frontier models scored in the single digits at release.
越难越窄：新基准只测旧基准刷不动的那一个尖。
Harder means narrower: each new test targets the one remaining peak.
评测方法大致分三派，每一派都有自己的偏差。
Evaluation comes in three schools, each with its own bias.
第一派是静态基准，选择题，判分完全自动。
The first is static benchmarks: multiple choice, fully automatic.
它便宜、可复现，但可以猜，也可能被污染。
Cheap and reproducible, but guessable and open to contamination.
第二派是人类盲评，Chatbot Arena 让用户匿名二选一。
The second is human blind rating: Arena shows two anonymous answers.
它最接近真实偏好，但它测的是喜欢，不是正确。
Closest to real preference, but it measures liking, not truth.
第三派是 LLM-as-judge，用更强的模型来打分。
The third is LLM-as-judge: a stronger model hands out the score.
它便宜、可扩展，和人类判断的相关性还不错。
Cheap, scalable, and decently correlated with human judgment.
让模型当裁判，先要承认它自己有偏好。
Let a model judge, and admit it has preferences of its own.
它偏爱排在前面的答案，这叫位置偏好。
It favours the answer placed first: position bias.
它也偏爱更长的回答，哪怕信息并没有更多。
It favours longer answers, even when they carry no more information.
它还偏爱同家族模型的输出，和排版漂亮的答案。
It favours its own family, and answers that look well formatted.
解决办法不是换裁判，而是照搬人类的制度设计。
The fix is not a better judge but human-style institutions.
随机交换顺序、隐藏身份、多裁判投票，再用人类标注校准。
Randomize order, hide identity, poll judges, recalibrate on humans.
比偏差更硬的问题，是数据污染，也就是考试泄题。
Harder than bias is contamination: the exam paper leaked.
测试题和答案就在语料里，它不是会做，而是记得。
Test items and answers sit in the corpus. It remembers, it does not solve.
第一种检测是 n-gram 重叠，看题目和语料有没有重合。
First check: n-gram overlap between test items and corpus.
第二种是 canary 字符串，在测试集里埋一个独特标记。
Second: a canary string, a unique marker planted in the test set.
然后看模型会不会把这个标记原样复述出来。
Then see whether the model repeats that marker verbatim.
第三种是扰动测试：改数字、换名字，再问一遍。
Third: perturbation. Change numbers, swap names, ask again.
三种办法都只是间接检查，没人能保证题库干净。
All three are indirect checks. Nobody can certify a test set is clean.
真会做的模型仍然答对，靠记得的模型立刻露馅。
A model that can solve it still answers; one that memorized fails.
心理测量学留下三把尺子，看榜单时都用得上。
Psychometrics leaves three rulers, all useful on a leaderboard.
第一把是信度：同一个模型多测几次，分数稳不稳。
Reliability: test the same model again. Does the score hold?
第二把是效度：这个测试有没有测到它声称的能力。
Validity: does the test measure the ability it claims to measure?
最关键的是构念效度：你说是推理，它考的是记忆。
Construct validity is the crux: you claim reasoning, it tests recall.
第三把是生态效度：实验室任务能不能代表真实使用。
Ecological validity: does a lab task represent real use?
所以看到高分，先问它到底测的是哪一种能力。
So when you see a high score, first ask which ability it measured.
这一问比分数本身有用得多，也更难回答。
That question is worth more than the score, and harder to answer.
幻觉是模型生成看似合理，实则错误的内容。
A hallucination looks plausible and is wrong or unsupported.
第一类是事实性幻觉：它把世界上的事情说错了。
Factuality errors get the world wrong.
比如爱因斯坦 1955 年出生，年份完全错位。
Einstein was born in 1955? The year is simply off.
第二类是忠实性幻觉：它偏离了你给的输入。
Faithfulness errors drift away from the input you gave.
让你总结一篇文章，它加进文章里没有的内容。
Asked to summarize, it adds material the article never contained.
还有一类是自洽性：同一个问题，两次回答互相矛盾。
A third kind: two answers to one question contradict each other.
共同点是，它擅长编故事，却从不标记这是我编的。
The common thread: it tells stories and never flags them as invented.
幻觉不是偶然的故障，而是训练方式的结构性副产品。
Hallucination is not a random fault. It is structural to training.
第一，目标不匹配：训练只奖励预测下一个词。
First, the objective is mismatched: training rewards the next word.
语料里像答案的文本更常见，于是它学会了自信补全。
Answer-shaped text beats I don't know, so it completes confidently.
第二，训练数据本身就有错误和过时的信息。
Second, the training data itself holds errors and stale facts.
第三，采样会选到低概率的词，偶尔就编了。
Third, sampling sometimes picks a low-probability token and invents.
第四，人类评分者偏爱有问必答，模型就少说不知道。
Fourth, raters prefer an answer to no answer, so it stops saying so.
它也没有知识边界的显式表示，不知道自己不知道。
It also has no explicit representation of where its knowledge ends.
校准问的是：它说九成把握，实际就对九成吗。
Calibration asks: when it says ninety percent, is it right that often?
完美校准的模型，置信度和准确率画出来是一条对角线。
A calibrated model plots confidence against accuracy on the diagonal.
实际模型常常过度自信：说九成五，只对七成。
Real models are overconfident: ninety-five claimed, seventy delivered.
ECE 把预测按置信度分桶，桶里比较两个数。
ECE buckets predictions by confidence and compares two numbers.
一个是平均置信度，一个是实际准确率，差距取绝对值。
Mean confidence versus accuracy, difference in absolute value.
再按每个桶的样本量加权平均，就得到 ECE。
Weight each bucket by its share of samples and average: that is ECE.
气象预报早就回答过：关键不是多自信，而是自信可信。
Weather forecasting learned it: value is not confidence, but trust.
这就是 Goodhart 定律的评测版。
This is the evaluation edition of Goodhart's law.
当一个指标成为目标，它就不再是好指标。
When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.
教育测量早就演过一遍：考试成了目标，教学变成刷题。
Education ran it: make exams the goal and teaching becomes drilling.
基准也一样：刷分成了目标，分数就不再代表能力。
Benchmarks too: once score-chasing is the goal, scores stop meaning ability.
于是模型学会的是考试技巧，而不是真本事。
So the model learns exam tricks instead of real skill.
这不是谁作弊，而是指标一旦可优化，就会被优化。
Nobody cheats. A metric that can be optimized will be optimized.
所以看到超越人类这种标题，先别急着转发。
So when a headline says it beats humans, do not share it yet.
第一问：这个基准测的到底是什么能力。
Question one: what ability does this benchmark actually test?
第二问：题库有没有污染，答案很可能是有的。
Question two: is the test set contaminated? Very likely yes.
第三问：人类基线是多少，又是谁测出来的。
Question three: what is the human baseline, and who measured it?
MMLU 的人类专家约百分之八十九点八，那是一批特定标注者的成绩。
MMLU human experts sit near 89.8 percent, a specific group of annotators.
第四问：分数提高，对应真实场景的什么改善。
Question four: what real-world improvement does the higher score imply?
问完这四个问题，标题通常就缩水一半。
Ask those four, and most headlines shrink by half.
这一章的主线只有一句：分数是代理，不是能力。
One line holds it together: a score is a proxy, not ability.
基准在军备竞赛，污染让分数贬值，幻觉是副产品。
Arms races, contamination, and hallucination as a by-product.
校准和构念效度，是看榜单时要戴的两副眼镜。
Calibration and construct validity are the lenses for leaderboards.
前面十二章，我们一直在外面看模型的行为。
For twelve chapters we have watched the model from the outside.
下一章把模型打开，看它内部到底在算什么。
Next we open it up and watch what it computes inside.
那就是机制可解释性，全课最像神经科学的一章。
That is mechanistic interpretability, the neuroscience-like chapter.
